items.title: Duffy Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 17, 1995
items.q: Two gentlemen, Ernie Wilkins and Sonny Rollins were unable to attend.

ctx.x: Would you like to tell us about what you were doing today?

This is the most incredible day of my life it seems, and I’ve had a few very interesting occasions in the history of music, being the son of a bass player. You know my dad, Chubby Jackson, has permitted me to exist in some very unique musical environments and situations, but today I was very, very honored to be part of a photograph for Life magazine of the greatest musicians of all time in the history of jazz. There were hundreds of them actually. I mean they were only supposed to have around maybe eighty…

thrill and honor just to stand in the background and watch them standing out on the street, freezing, you know, but taking a great photograph by the legendary Gordon Parks. And it was such a thrill just to be there.
